argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0101b: meeting "b" (functional design) of series SY0101.

PROJECT
The team is designing a voice-controlled kitchen timer.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Industrial Designer (ID)  Tomas  present
B  Marketing Expert (ME)  Grace  present
C  User Interface designer (UI)  Ravi  ABSENT, never speaks
D  Project Manager (PM)  Helen  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0101a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, introduced the team and presented the project: a voice-controlled kitchen timer that sits on the counter and can be operated hands-free. She presented the budget: a selling price of 25 euros, a maximum production cost of 12.50 euros per unit, and a profit target of 50 million euros. The team discussed the target group and first features. The final target group is home cooks. This replaced an earlier choice of professional kitchens, which the team revised because of the price point and the kitchen noise. The user interface designer raised the wake word problem, the alarm, and a simple display. The industrial designer pointed out that a custom wake word and a spoken alarm would increase the hardware cost. The project manager assigned research tasks to each team member. The next meeting, the functional design meeting, is in thirty minutes.
  decisions: The target group is home cooks in ordinary households. This was revised during the meeting from an earlier choice of professional kitchens. The timer will support multiple named timers. The display will use large, readable digits rather than a colour screen. The timer will have a physical button fallback in case voice commands are not recognised. The team will meet again in thirty minutes for the functional design meeting.
  actions: The marketing expert will research what home cooks need from a kitchen timer, possibly with a quick survey. The industrial designer will investigate voice recognition chips and whether they fit within the 12.50 euro production cost. He will also look at battery versus mains power. The user interface designer will work out the wake word, the voice commands (set, cancel, time remaining), the display and a button fallback. The project manager will send round the minutes.
  problems: It is unknown whether a voice recognition chip fits within the 12.50 euro production cost. The power source (battery or mains) is undecided, because always-on listening consumes power. It is undecided whether the wake word will be fixed or user-selectable. A user-selectable wake word needs a more expensive chip. It is undecided whether the alarm will announce which timer finished or only beep. A spoken alarm needs a speaker and adds cost. The device should be easy to clean and at least splash-proof, but this has not been specified further.
  action item SY0101a.ai1: Research user requirements for the kitchen timer among home cooks, possibly through a quick survey. This was originally assigned as research into chefs' needs. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0101a.ai2: Investigate available voice recognition chips and their cost relative to the 12.50 euro production budget, including battery versus mains power. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0101a.ai3: Design the wake word, the voice commands (set, cancel, time remaining), the display and a button fallback. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0101a.ai4: Send round the minutes of the kickoff meeting. (owner D, active)
  fact (plan_change): The team first agreed to target professional kitchens and restaurants. Later in the meeting they changed the target to home cooks, because of the 25 euro price point and the noise in professional kitchens.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed letting users choose their own wake word. This was not agreed because of the chip cost.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer suggested a fixed wake word to allow a cheap chip. The project manager only said to keep it in mind.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert proposed a spoken alarm that announces which timer is done. This was left open because it needs a speaker.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F1_ABSENT_DISCUSSED [F1]: One team member is absent. The others discuss them (why they are away, what they would think, what to tell them). The absent person never speaks. The gold summary must not attribute any statement to the absent person.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.
- F1_INTERLEAVED_TOPICS [F1]: Two agenda topics are discussed interleaved: the conversation switches back and forth between topic X and topic Y at least twice each. The gold summary must present each topic coherently.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
